A jury has been unable to reach a verdict for the second time over the 2021 gangland murder of Sydney underworld figure Bilal Hamze.

Samuel John Rokomaqisa faced a three-month trial accused of being the gunman, who killed Hamze or the getaway driver.

Rokomaqisa was found guilty of a failed attempt to kill Hamze's brother Ibrahem Hamze months after the murder.

A jury has been unable to reach a verdict for a second time in the Bilal Hamze murder trial.

The man accused of killing gangster Hamze in the Sydney CBD five years ago, Samuel John Rokomaqisa, now faces the prospect of a rare third murder trial in the Supreme Court.

Rokomaqisa was facing trial as either the gunman who took out Hamze or the getaway driver fleeing with the hitman from the scene on June 17, 2021.

Hamze died in a hail of bullets after his killer fired on him from a car as he left Kid Kyoto restaurant near Bridge Street with a sex worker.

Dashcam vision captured the moment Mr Hamze's killer circled back to look at his lifeless body before fleeing. (Supplied)

Graphic CCTV footage played to the jury showed the gunman shoot Hamze, circle back and fire again before pulling up a third time to the curb near his lifeless body.

On Friday, after deliberating for 11 days, the jury was unable to reach a unanimous verdict on the charge of murder and were discharged.

However, Rokomaqisa was found guilty over a failed attempt to kill Hamze's brother Ibrahem Hamze at North Sydney months later in November 2021.

Mr Hamze's funeral, which was followed by the burials of three more of his family. (AAP)

The three-month trial explored one of the deadliest chapters in Sydney's criminal history.

Hamze's death was one of seven in 18 months of violence at the height of the Alameddine crime family's war with the Hamzys.

The two gangs had been locked in a feud over control of Sydney's drug trade at the time.

Police had deployed rarely used non-association powers, dubbed Serious Crime Prevention Orders, to calm the bloodshed between the two clans.

Mr Hamze inside Kid Kyoto restaurant before he was shot dead. (Supplied)

But Hamze would be followed to the grave by relatives Salim Hamze, Toufik Hamze and Ghassan Amoun during a wave of violence that plagued the city.
